I would be delighted to assist you with auditing your existing or new HubSpot module. To get started effectively, please share detailed information on what specific aspect of the module you need assistance with, such as functionality checks, performance analysis, compatibility with current versions of HubSpot, and any error messages you're encountering.

Please provide the following details:
- A brief description of the module's purpose or feature it is supposed to perform.
- Any specific issues or problems you are experiencing related to this module.
- Any relevant screenshots or logs that might help diagnose the issue.

Your input will enable us to tailor a precise audit and solution. Thank you for your patience and cooperation!

HubSpot Markup Language (HubL) is a custom syntax that enables developers to add features specific to your website or application directly into the main content of your web pages using Markdown formatting. This allows for cleaner, more semantic markup that integrates well with HTML and CSS.

Here’s an example of how you might use HubL:

```markdown
---
title: My Page Title
---

# Introduction

This is a [header1](https://example.com/header1) section.

## Subsection 1

Subsection content goes here. Use *italic* or **bold** text for emphasis.

### Nested Section

Nested section example:
- Item 1
- Item 2

You can also use [links](https://www.example.com/), [code blocks](#),
and even include images with:

![Alt Text](http://example/image.jpg)

## Table of Contents
---
* Introduction
* Subsection 1
* Nested Section
```

### Markdown in HubL Examples:
Markdown syntax can be used directly within a header or paragraph to format text. Here’s an example where Markdown is utilized for formatting:

```markdown
---

# Header with Markdown

Here's some markdown code to format the header and section:

- **Bold**: `**This is bold text**`
- *Italic*: `*This is italic text*`

```

### Link Example:
Links can be created using HTML attributes within HubL, like this:

```markdown
[Link](http://example.com)

Or you can create an internal link to another part of the same page:

[Internal Link](#section1)
```

Remember that HubL is intended for web pages and not necessarily every element on a web page. It’s best used within header elements or after markdown links.
